issues.title: cookie-get returns JSON object but localstorage-get returns raw value — inconsistent output format

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
1. ./b4w.ps1 cookie-get theme
2. ./b4w.ps1 localstorage-get user_prefs
Compare the output formats.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Both 'get' commands should return consistently-formatted output, either both as raw values or both as structured objects with metadata.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: cookie-get returns a JSON object with name, value, domain, path, expires, httpOnly, secure, sameSite fields. localstorage-get returns only the raw value string (e.g., '{"lang":"en","tz":"UTC"}'). sessionstorage-get also returns raw value. This means scripts parsing 'get' output need to handle two different formats depending on storage type.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: Cookies have structured metadata (domain, path, expires, flags) that naturally maps to a JSON object, whereas localStorage/sessionStorage are simple key-value stores. However, the CLI could still wrap localStorage values in a consistent envelope like {"key": "...", "value": "..."} for uniform machine parsing.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Wrap localstorage-get and sessionstorage-get output in a JSON envelope: {"key": "...", "value": "..."} to match the structured pattern of cookie-get
- Or add a --value-only flag to cookie-get for users who only want the value, making both modes available
- Document the output format of each 'get' command in their --help text so users know what to expect before running

issues.title: cookie-set does not echo back applied properties — no way to verify flags took effect without a separate cookie-get

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 cookie-set session_id abc123 --domain localhost --path / --httpOnly --secure

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Output confirms all flags that were applied, e.g., 'Cookie set: session_id (domain=localhost, path=/, httpOnly, secure)'

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Output is just 'Cookie set: session_id' — no indication of which flags were applied. If a flag was silently ignored due to a typo (e.g., --httpOnly misspelled), the user would not notice without running cookie-get.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The cookie-set success message is generated from only the cookie name, without including the resolved cookie attributes. The backend likely sets the cookie successfully but the CLI output doesn't reflect the full cookie object.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Echo back key cookie properties in the success message: domain, path, httpOnly, secure, sameSite, expires
- This provides immediate feedback and helps catch typos in flag names (e.g., --httponly vs --httpOnly)
- Same pattern would benefit localstorage-set and sessionstorage-set (echo the key and value truncated if long)

issues.title: Dev wrappers (./b4w.ps1, ./b4w.sh) not mentioned in --help output for in-repo usage

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Run ./b4w.ps1 help and search for 'b4w' or './b4w.ps1'

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Help output mentions the dev wrapper scripts for users working inside the repository.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Help output only shows 'Dev mode: cargo run --manifest-path cli/browser4-cli/Cargo.toml -- <command>' at the very bottom. It does not mention ./b4w.ps1 or ./b4w.sh. A new contributor would need to read CLAUDE.md or SKILL.md to discover these wrappers.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The help text is generated from the CLI binary's clap definitions, which describe the installed binary (browser4-cli). The dev wrappers are repo-level convenience scripts that live outside the binary's help system.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Add a 'Dev wrappers' note in the Quick Start section of --help mentioning ./b4w.ps1 and ./b4w.sh
- Or add a post-build step that injects repo-specific usage notes into the help text when built from source
- The SKILL.md already documents this; linking to it from --help would help

issues.title: cookie-list --domain uses exact match only — no substring or pattern matching

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 cookie-list --domain localhost (works with exact match). Try --domain local (partial match) — returns empty array even if localhost cookies exist.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Documentation clearly states it's an exact match, but a --domain-pattern or wildcard support would be more flexible for users managing cookies across subdomains.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Exact domain match only. This is documented correctly in --help ('Only include cookies with the exact domain'), so it's not a bug — but it limits usefulness for subdomain scenarios.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The --domain flag performs an exact string match against the cookie's domain field. While correct for the documented behavior, many real-world scenarios involve subdomain patterns (e.g., .example.com matching app.example.com).

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Consider adding a --domain-suffix flag for subdomain matching (e.g., --domain-suffix example.com matches app.example.com, api.example.com)
- Or support glob patterns in --domain (e.g., --domain '*.example.com')
- At minimum, document the exact-match behavior prominently with an example showing why a partial match returns nothing
